Traced instruction-by-instruction from games/gs1/asm/080a93a4.s (500 bytes, no automatic family-transplant workspace since this owner scored below threshold). Signature s32 Func_080a93a4(s32 arg0, s32 arg1, void *ctx): arg1 is dead (overwritten before first read, matching the 080a5614/080a6a98 sibling convention exactly). ctx is a small selection-cursor struct: ctx+8=page (party-member/character index), ctx+16=selected slot (0..4), ctx+24=page*5+slot written back on every call (proved identical in games/gs1/recon/en/main/080a6a98.c and 080a5614.c, and independently reconstructed by m2c from the raw .s with the same field offsets).

menu = Data_03001f2c (same global as select_quantity.c, update_compatibility_indicators.c, start_compatibility_indicators.c, 080a9598.c and both loop siblings). menu+44 and menu+48 are two distinct window handles (menu+44 used with Func_08015270/UiWindow_Commit and as the Func_08015080/UiText_DrawAt window arg; menu+48 used as the object arg to every Func_080a2268/Render_SetTilemapFlagRect call in the second half of the function). menu+456 is a u16 item-id table indexed by page*5+slot (2 bytes/slot, 5 slots/page) -- the same table and stride used by 080a9598.c, 080a5614.c, 080a6a98.c and equipment_menu/update_compatibility_indicators.c (which indexes an adjacent-purpose table at menu+520 with the same *2 stride).

Body, in order: (1) recompute ctx+24, UiWindow_Commit(menu+44), WaitFrames(1); (2) if the item at menu+456+ctx24*2 is nonzero, UiText_DrawAt(masked-id + (s32)&Value_00000075, menu+44, 0, 0) -- a one-shot tooltip/status line, exactly mirroring 080a5614.c's use of the same Value_00000075 base; (3) a 5-iteration row loop (row 0..4, y=1,3,5,7,9): for the selected row reread the ctx24-indexed item, for the other four walk a u16* pointer seeded at menu+456+page*5*2 and advanced every iteration regardless of branch taken (matches the reference's unconditional r9+=2 at the loop bottom); each row calls Item_GetData(id & 0x1ff) and reads a 4-byte word at offset +0x14 of the returned pointer (raw byte offset, deliberately not routed through item.h's named `struct ItemDefinition` since that header's byte-accurate field at 0x14 is the 1-byte `element` -- the reference emits a genuine 32-bit `ldr`, not `ldrb`, at this site, so a word-at-+20 read is what the assembly actually proves, not a claim about a wider field name); type==4 draws an empty-slot marker (width 14), otherwise UiText_DrawAt-style Func_08015280(arg0, type+1, 27, y, style) draws an icon (style 0 for the selected row, 4 otherwise) before a width-13 marker; (4) a second, unrelated 4-iteration loop over menu+48 drawing fixed width-12/height-1/field-15 markers at y=1,3,5,7; (5) a final compatibility check: reread menu+456+ctx24*2, and if bit 0x200 is set, look up the item again and switch on its byte-2 `type` field (matches item.h's ItemDefinition.type at offset 2 exactly) with cases 1/2/3/4 each drawing one more menu+48 marker at width 12, field 14, and y=1/7/5/3 respectively (a non-monotonic case->row mapping read directly off the reference's branch targets, not inferred).

m2c's own reconstruction from the raw assembly (via the project's workbench: `compiler workbench`, run after a temporary name-only source-paths.json entry to satisfy its registration requirement, reverted afterward since this owner is not adopted) independently produced the same field offsets (ctx+8/16/24, menu+44/48/456), the same +0x14 word read after Item_GetData, and the same y=1/3/5/7 case->row mapping for the final switch, which cross-checks the hand trace above; m2c's own attempt to compile that draft failed only on missing type context for two of the switch cases sharing a merged block (a decompiler limitation, not evidence of a different shape).

Current state: differing_halfwords=227, wrong_instructions=181, candidate 512 bytes vs reference 500 (matched_prefix=7, i.e. only the fixed callee-save prologue lines up before the first divergence). The single largest driver is a whole-function register-role swap: the reference keeps `menu` in r8 and `ctx` in sl for the entire function, while every C phrasing tried here (original combined-expression field access, an explicit reused `base5 = ctx->8*5` local matching the reference's own r9-reuse of that subexpression, reordering the ctx-field-read vs menu-deref statement to lead with either one, and copying `ctx` into a fresh local before first use) makes the compiler choose the opposite assignment (`ctx`->r8, `menu`->r7) instead, with zero change in the resulting differing_halfwords/wrong_instructions count across every variant tried (227/181 in all cases but one: the base5 local alone measured slightly worse at 243/191, so it was reverted). Because r8 and sl carry the base pointers for essentially every field access in the function, this one role swap cascades into a renumbered register on nearly every subsequent instruction, which is why the --align view reports almost the entire function body as mismatched even though the control flow, field offsets, constants and call arguments were independently confirmed correct against both the raw assembly and m2c's read of it.

This is the same class of residual the two closer siblings (080a5614.c, 080a6a98.c) already documented as 'register-role choices ... coupled through the compiler's whole-function register allocation, not independently tunable' after real iteration on materially simpler owners; per Cleanroom's inversion guidance this owner was not pushed into an open-ended search on that residual. No PERM_GENERAL/PERM_INT permutation search or register hints were used (none are appropriate pre-structural-convergence, and hand-forcing register assignment is disallowed outright).
